column1: # The BASKET ruler: what a cross-section of real single names looks like, at three levels, for the
# `-basket` channel (N equity names as observational second-pass instances of the primary).  The
# graded rows are SMH's eight largest holdings as of 2026-10-02 -- NVDA TSM AMD AVGO MU INTC AMAT
# KLAC -- held fixed so the bands compare across releases, over 2012-01-04..2026-08-31 (3685
# sessions): daily adjusted closes from Yahoo's public chart API, LOG returns.  `BasketAnchorSuite` /
# `basket_anchor_tests` re-derive the graded bands from the `eight` rows; editing a row moves the
# Conventions.  vol = sd (n - 1) of daily log returns x sqrt(252), %.  gaps10 / gaps5 = sessions
# with |r| > 10% / 5% per 252 sessions.  maxDD = deepest peak-to-trough decline, %.  d10 / d20 =
# share of sessions more than 10% / 20% below the running peak.  acf1 = lag-1 autocorrelation of
# |r|.  kurt = daily kurtosis (not excess).  The basket is the EQUAL-WEIGHT mean of the members'
# simple returns, as a log series.  pairCorr = the 28 pairwise correlations of daily log returns.
# idioShare = 1 - R^2 of a name on SMH.  tailCoincidence = on the basket's worst-1% sessions, the
# share of names below their own 1% cut.  The mechanism rows split sessions by SPY's return: its
# worst and best deciles, and its central 45-55%.  Eras: 2012-2019 and 2020-2026.
# LEVEL 1 grades a name against a population of names, not an index: the eight run 1.9-3.4x SPY's
# volatility (16.6%) and gap an order of magnitude more often (SPY: 0.1 sessions/yr past 10%).
# LEVEL 2 is the basket's relation to its group index (SMH) and to the market -- SPY for the S&P
# anchor set, QQQ for the Nasdaq set: in the model, which has no sector index, the basket's
# aggregate IS the sector, and the `corrSpy`/`betaOnSpy`/`volRatioSpy` rows (or their `Qqq`
# counterparts) are the relation it is graded on, per anchor set; level 1's vol ratio reads
# against the set's primary vol (`SPY vol` / `QQQ vol`).  LEVEL 3 is what a basket rule reads.
# SURVIVORSHIP.  A list taken today holds names that grew into the index's top, so their time below
# peak and their drift describe winners: the names' d20 is reported, not graded, and `-basketdrift`
# The "aggregate clusters more than its members" check is NOT clean in the record (by era the basket
# sits inside the members' range), so the acf1 rows are readings, not a gate.
